# ob-02 — Make CLI credential entry safe by default

Reduce accidental passphrase exposure in CLI use. Keep environment, file, and stdin inputs available; decide whether the inline `--passphrase` option should be removed or explicitly deprecated, and document the resulting workflow.

**Findings:** Obfuscator.Cli/ObfuscatorCliProgram.cs; README.md; Obfuscator.Cli/README.md (was S02) · **Size:** M · **Tree:** cli,docs

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

The CLI accepts --passphrase, which can expose the secret in process listings. Environment, file, and stdin inputs already exist and the documentation recommends them.

## Files

Obfuscator.Cli/ObfuscatorCliProgram.cs; Obfuscator.Tests/ObfuscatorTests.cs; README.md; Obfuscator.Cli/README.md.

## Failing tests

Add CLI coverage that environment, passphrase-file, and passphrase-stdin inputs continue to work. Add a case proving inline --passphrase is rejected and does not echo a supplied secret.

## Implement

Remove the CLI --passphrase option and its resolver branch; retain the library Passphrase API. Keep environment, file, and stdin mechanisms. Update usage text and docs to direct users to those inputs.

## Check

Run focused CLI credential tests and the full solution test suite. Check help output and all docs for stale inline-passphrase examples.

## Git

Do not include real passphrases in tests, fixtures, output, or commit messages.
